title: NOAA tide flooding
summary: Retrospective classification of NOAA’s official minor-flood flag for day D+1 using a station-day row dated D, under documented timing and access restrictions.

post.title: A prediction task from NOAA's tide gauges
paragraphs: The frozen panel covers 122 NOS stations. For row date D, the build attaches NOAA’s official minor-flood flag for D+1. It is not defined by simply thresholding the raw maximum. Current documentation corrects the earlier same-day and raw-threshold descriptions; original data and tags remain unchanged.

Two split designs are available: temporal and station-disjoint. The latter excludes its evaluation stations from training. Recorded baseline comparisons describe those particular splits; they do not certify future operational performance or establish an optimal honest-model limit.

The baseline scripts use ordinary train-fitted XGBoost and do not implement the demonstrated reverse-history attack. The original scoring interface nevertheless supplied a complete feature frame. Interpret recorded results with the documented vintage, timing and access limitations, and use AUC alongside class-balance information.

limitations: A derived research dataset from NOAA CO-OPS public-domain data, labelled as derived - not an official NOAA, NOS or NWS product, and not a flood warning or forecast service.
About 2% of station-days are positive. Accuracy is misleading on this task by a wide margin.
The holdout is labelled and downloadable. Keep its labels outside the evaluated agent's workspace during an evaluation.

No claim of real-time or operational forecasting validity: historical feature and label availability at the prediction instant is assumed from a current source snapshot, not verified against release vintages.

Documentation correction: the build assigns NOAA's official minor-flood flag to the day after the measured maximum; the earlier description of a same-day flag was wrong. The frozen data and tags are unchanged.

The labeled eval split is development/validation. Final holdout scoring requires prediction-time access restrictions; the original scorer provided the complete feature frame. Downloadable holdout labels must stay outside model development.
baseline_scope: one baseline only. No coding agent and no harness comparison was run, and none is implied.
